label: PF Backlog 597
title: EDP-16: Object lifecycle (versioning/lock/retention), signed-URL policy, delete/replica/backup reconciliation
body: Part of EPIC BI-PF-1292. Source: docs/Product_Forge_Enterprise_Performance_Security_DB_Storage_Roadmap.md. Phase item (see epic). Language rule L1 = Go; must pass scripts/dev/language_rule_review.py.

brief.problem: Objects have no lifecycle/retention/lock guarantees and ad-hoc URLs bypass policy
brief.why: Enterprise compliance and safe delete/backup semantics

objective: Define and enforce object lifecycle rules (versioning, lock, retention), signed-URL access policy, and delete/replica/backup reconciliation across the storage layer.
acceptance_criteria: Lifecycle/lock/retention capabilities expressed on ObjectStore interface and implemented in S3 adapter
Signed-URL policy central minting with TTL bounds enforced
Delete/replica/backup reconciliation job detects and reports drift vs manifest
Conformance tests cover lifecycle behavior per provider
Language rule L1 (Go-capable) review passes
approach: Interface-first: add optional LifecycleCapable/Capability assertions, implement per-provider, wire manifest validation into reconciliation.
risks: Provider capability gaps (local filesystem, non-S3) for object-lock/versioning
Retention rules conflicting with residency/backup retention
rollback: Feature-flag lifecycle enforcement; providers without capability degrade to no-op with warning.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend the provider-neutral ObjectStore interface (BI-PF-1299) and S3 adapter (BI-PF-1306) with lifecycle capabilities: versioning, object-lock/legal-hold, retention rules, signed-URL policy; reconcile deletes/replicas/backups via residency manifest from BI-PF-1304.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES BI-PF-1306 S3 adapter at done
REQUIRES BI-PF-1304 residency manifest at done
conflict_findings: Low: S3 adapter (BI-PF-1306) files may still be warm; coordinate interface changes
duplication_findings: core/lock_manager.py is an in-process lock, not bucket object-lock — pattern reuse only, no duplication
No existing object lifecycle/signed-URL code in candidates; core/*_policy.py files are governance policies (different domain)
analysis.rationale: Builds directly on existing storage interfaces/adapter; adds capability layer rather than new component. Reuse-first honored.
assumptions: Lifecycle features are optional capabilities on ObjectStore interface
Signed URLs are minted centrally, never stored
Manifest from BI-PF-1304 is authoritative for allowed regions
risks: Provider capability gaps (local filesystem, non-S3) for object-lock/versioning
Retention rules conflicting with residency/backup retention
missing_info: Default retention periods per data class
Whether object-lock applies in dev/local mode
Signed-URL TTL ceiling and audience model

context_review.reason: Interfaces, adapter, and manifest exist or are pinned; only policy values need human input.
